## Incident Report — MTA 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

### Evidence reviewed
- `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,091 frames, ~21:32–22:32 capture window, IP `172.17.0.99` is the sole internal host generating traffic)
- `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` (Suricata/ET alert export)

### Victim host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.17.0.99** | Source of all outbound traffic; consistent across all artifacts below |
| MAC | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==172.17.0.99`) and DHCP client MAC, both agree |
| Hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** | DHCP `dhcp.option.hostname`; corroborated by NBNS name registrations and DNS queries for `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT.bepositive.com` |
| Domain | `bepositive.com` (AD domain; DC = `WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19` / 172.17.0.17) | LDAP/Kerberos/CLDAP SRV lookups, NBNS `WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19<20>` |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** | Kerberos `CNameString` in both AS-REQ (client→172.17.0.17) and reply traffic, realm `BEPOSITIVE.COM` |

### Malware family and attribution
**Win32/Koi Stealer** — **signature-confirmed.**

- ET/Suricata fired `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (48 hits) directly on the POST traffic to `79.124.78.197`.
- Behaviorally corroborated: `tcp.stream 48` (frame 1668 onward) shows repeated `POST /foots.php HTTP/1.1` to `79.124.78.197` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, a spoofed `User-Agent: Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; ... Windows NT 10.0 ...)` (IE7 UA on a Win10 host — a stealer/loader fingerprint mismatch, not a real browser), and a pipe-delimited beacon body pattern, e.g.:
  - `101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|f3f3oMg2lz4XGyHy0LidzFiNvSftke//k+COyrO9aBI=`
  - `111|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|XHfhyxOtsArXQLiP|<binary blob>`
  - `102|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`
  
  The GUID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654` is a stable bot/victim ID reused across ~48 check-ins between 21:35:06 and 22:31:55 (capture-local time).
- No initial infection/delivery stage (dropper, exploit doc, initial download) is present in this capture — the pcap begins mid-infection, capturing only the ongoing C2 beacon/exfil traffic.

### Indicators of compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `79.124.78.197:80` — evidence: `tcp.stream 48/51` and ~48 signature-matched POSTs; contacted by **bare IP with no preceding DNS resolution** for `79.124.78.197` anywhere in the capture, a strong C2 tell.

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` — repeated beacon/exfil POST endpoint (Koi Stealer check-in, signature match)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — GET, stream 51; response includes affiliate/click ID `qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php` — pay-per-install/loader-style check-in pattern
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` — subsequent POST on the same stream with an encrypted/binary body, 105-byte payload

**Domains**
- None. The C2 host was never resolved via DNS in this capture; all contact with `79.124.78.197` was by literal IP address.

**Transferred files / hashes**
- No executable or payload file was observed being transferred over HTTP, SMB, or any other protocol in this capture (`--export-objects http` yielded only empty POST bodies for `foots.php`, the benign `connecttest.txt`, and Adobe's `ProcessMAU.txt` — none are malicious artifacts). No file-hash IOC can be grounded from this evidence; the infection vector and any dropped binary occurred outside the capture window.

### Benign context (do not treat as IOCs)
- `www.msftconnecttest.com` (23.220.251.149/158) — Windows NCSI connectivity check
- `acroipm2.adobe.com` — legitimate Adobe ARM update-manager check-in
- `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `x1.c.lencr.org` — Windows CryptoAPI certificate/CTL revocation checks
- Microsoft telemetry/service domains: `*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `officeclient.microsoft.com`, `odc.officeapps.live.com`, `ecs.office.com`, `client.wns.windows.com`, MSN/Bing domains, `weathermapdata.blob.core.windows.net`
- `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201, TLS SNI) — large (701 KB) but ordinary encrypted web traffic to an Italian bakery site; no alert fired on it and no evidence ties it to the infection
- `sso.godaddy.com` (23.195.212.189) — routine TLS session
- SMB/Kerberos/LDAP/DCERPC traffic between `172.17.0.99` and the domain controller `172.17.0.17` — this triggered several legacy GPL rules (`SMB NTLMSSP overflow attempt`, `SMB_COM_TRANSACTION Max Data Count of 0`, `kerberos principal name overflow`). These are standard Windows AD authentication/session-setup exchanges (SMBv1 negotiate, NTLMSSP auth, IPC$ share access, Kerberos AS-REQ); the packet contents show normal domain logon behavior, not exploitation. Assessed as legacy-signature false positives on benign AD traffic, not evidence of lateral movement.

### Incident summary
The Windows workstation `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT` (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged on as domain user `afletcher` on the `bepositive.com` AD domain, is infected with **Win32/Koi Stealer** (signature-confirmed by ET rule). Starting at 21:35 (capture-local), the host began beaconing to its C2 at `79.124.78.197:80` via bare-IP HTTP POSTs to `/foots.php` and `/index.php`, using a spoofed IE7 user-agent and a consistent bot GUID, repeating roughly every 1-2 minutes for the remainder of the one-hour capture. No dropper, exploit stage, or downloaded payload is present in this capture, so the delivery mechanism could not be determined from this evidence alone.
